body:
> I'm not sure this note is necessary. I understand the frustration, but... I personally see little ambiguity or confusion over this. Nowhere it is implied that the scene tree would unpause itself when calling `change_scene_to_file` & co., nor it is exhaustive, as the current scene can be also changed with a corresponding property. 

That's something that is quite obvious indeed when you realize the issue, the problem is realizing the issue. Normally I think you would see things completely stopped and the issue would be more obvious, but in my case I believe I just lucked out because the menu that worked just stopped working.

> The note is also way too long for basically saying "_This property is unaffected when the scene is changed_" which, I reiterate, I believe there's little confusion for.

I can reduce the text, that's fine.

> Instead of adding a note, if there's something in the documentation, or any other aspect of the engine, that made you believe in this behavior, that's what should be addressed.
> 
> ... Could it be the wording of `change_scene_to_file()` and similar? Had I written this description, I would've not said the following:
> 
> > Changes the running scene to the one at the given [param path]

> Perhaps the confusion stems from "the **running** scene", as it may imply the scene "begins running again" as soon as it is changed. It should've just said "the current scene", because that's what it is.

It actually added to my confusion that I already had previously, yes. Should I close this PR and open a new one or just pivot this PR? I would still prefer to add the note to paused tho because it's what caused the odd behaviour in the end tho.
